decisions.reason: The question asks whether SiT captures real-world pedestrian–robot interactions. It omits how the dataset supports pedestrian perception and motion prediction for social navigation.

The method mentions a mobile robot and indoor and outdoor scenes. It omits manual operation, crowded locations in Seoul, the two 3D LiDARs and five cameras, pulse-per-second synchronization, and 360-degree camera coverage.
The method gives 20-second sequences at 10 Hz. It omits the counts of scenes, images, and point-cloud frames, as well as 2D and 3D box annotations, object IDs, and multilayer semantic maps.
The poster omits ego-motion compensation and the use of distinct scenes in the training, validation, and test subsets.
The finding and caption define both interaction criteria and report that SiT has more instances satisfying both. Panel (b) names Waymo Open, Argoverse 2, and nuScenes in its legend.
The poster omits the detection and tracking baselines, the center-distance thresholds used to calculate detection mAP, and the tracking metrics.

The method gives 9 seconds of trajectory data per sample but omits the 2-second history and 7-second forecast split, minimum ADE and FDE at 5 and 20 candidates, the forecasting baselines, and the reported semantic-map gains.
The poster omits the 7-second end-to-end benchmark from raw sensor data to future 3D boxes and trajectories, the compared models, and the four evaluation metrics.
The poster omits the authors’ statement that time constraints prevented collection at the scale of hundreds of thousands of frames.

notes: The figure legends and axis labels are readable at the supplied image size, though small relative to the poster text. The headings and placement of the figure below the finding make the reading order clear. The checklist confirms the 20-second duration, 10 Hz sampling rate, and 2-meter threshold. Its 2-second history and 7-second future are consistent with the stated 9-second sample duration. The supplied evidence does not establish whether “significantly higher” refers to a formal statistical test.
